title: Actual scalar mate under the support realizations
statement: Fix the same finite-field and compactification setting [def-pur-conventions, def-weil-compactifications-refinements], finite extensions E,F of Q_l, a coefficient inclusion i, and a positive ramification exponent e with the actual principal-ideal equation. Let SE,SF be reduction/total-limit calculi. For every complete bounded constructible finite-Tor E input M, its scalar extension CM is a complete bounded constructible finite-Tor F input. Under the uniquely normalized support realizations [lem-pur-compact-support-projection-realization], extension of the E realization followed by the specified completed scalar arrow [def-pur-compact-support-completed-scalar-arrow] equals the actual proper/open scalar mate comparison followed by the F realization. This is equality of integral morphisms, detected on this constructible domain by the Milnor injection, not a faithfulness assertion for arbitrary derived reductions.

proof.text: B3: gamma_identification follows from the finite reduction equation already supplied by compactSupportScalarLimitReduction. Its normalized unique scalar arrow is the chosen completedArrow. The generic comparison_reduction equation identifies the finite reductions of the other composite. The proved comparison_factorization identifies its finite comparison with the ordered proper/open finiteTensorMap, and naturality of scalarReductionBalancing moves the E realization through that equation. Both realizations have their prescribed finite counits. After cancelling the invertible target finite counit and finite balancing isomorphism, the two maps therefore have equal reductions at exponents e(n+1). The source is constructible by the qcqs realization and finite-free coefficient model, and the target is constructible via the F realization. For an arbitrary exponent n+1 choose e(n+1), and use naturality of the reduction unit and the transition in the target reduction cone to descend equality to exponent n+1. The same constructible Milnor injection proves equality of integral maps. The integral residue-Tor criterion supplies the scalar-extended finite-Tor witness. No extra theorem hole is introduced, and no arbitrary reduction faithfulness is assumed.
